evidence: app/server.mjs:88 — abilities route is one self-contained handler
app/src/views.mjs:250 — renderAbilityPage is one deletable function
app/src/views.mjs:602 — renderAbilityPageByName is dead code that would linger
app/src/views.mjs:560 — abilities links live only inside renderPokemonPage's own section
removability.rationale: Features are route+view pairs with no cross-file entanglement; removal is a handful of scattered edits across two files rather than delete-and-done, partly because dead wrappers obscure what's actually used.

evidence: app/src/render.mjs:66-77 — every Pokémon card sprite rendered in one function
app/src/api.mjs:46 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL construction point
app/src/views.mjs:283-305 — sortRows is the single sorting implementation for move tables
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious, findable place and cover every list because all cards flow through pokemonCard/cardGrid. The exception is card-list derivation, which is reimplemented per view and would force N-place fixes for anything needing richer card data.

evidence: app/server.mjs:55 — htmx partial detection isolated in the server layer
app/src/views.mjs:87 — views take an explicit partial flag, keeping fragments reusable
app/server.mjs:73-93 — server assembles data for types/moves/abilities routes
app/src/views.mjs:37 — but home/pokemon data assembly lives in the views module instead
app/src/render.mjs:1 — presentation layer imports spriteUrl, which is tied to API_BASE_URL
coupling.rationale: Layering exists and the htmx seam is clean, but the fetch-then-render responsibility is split inconsistently between server.mjs and views.mjs, and views.mjs mixes data assembly with rendering.

evidence: app/src/render.mjs:79-81 — cardGrid stretches across home/type/move/ability lists
app/src/views.mjs:139-150 — dedupeSortedPokemonEntries helps but only covers part of the card-list shape
app/src/views.mjs:255-263 — ability page hand-rolls its own id/hidden map instead of the shared helper
app/src/views.mjs:596-613 — three *ByName wrappers built then never wired up
abstraction_design.rationale: The small primitives are well designed, but the app's most-repeated shape (cards from Pokémon references) is copy-pasted with per-view variations, and an intended page-level abstraction was abandoned half-built.

findings.issue: Turning API Pokémon references into card descriptors is reimplemented in renderTypePage, renderMovePage (223-235) and renderAbilityPage (255-276) with three different idioms (one keeps a fallback-name branch, one hand-rolls its own id map).
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper, e.g. pokemonCardsFromReferences(entries, speciesCatalog), so ordering, dedupe and sprite/id resolution have a single home; new card lists and card-level fixes then land in one place.

findings.issue: renderMovePageByName/renderAbilityPageByName/renderTypePageByName are dead code that duplicate the fetch-then-render logic server.mjs inlines at 73-93, misleading future editors about where to change behavior.
findings.suggestion: Either use the wrappers from the routes (making views own data assembly consistently) or delete them.

findings.issue: All HTML is built by string concatenation with a hand-rolled escapeHtml that every interpolation must remember to call; one missed call is an injection bug, and this scales poorly as templates grow.
findings.suggestion: Use Hono's current html`` tagged template from 'hono/html' (auto-escapes by default, raw for trusted fragments) for the whole render layer.

findings.issue: Route handlers for types/moves/abilities fetch data inline while home and pokemon routes delegate to getHomeData/getPokemonPageData in views.mjs, so the same responsibility lives in two layers.
findings.suggestion: Pick one convention — e.g. every route calls a getXPageData in the views/data layer — and apply it uniformly.

findings.issue: Three separate caching mechanisms (fetchJson cache/pending at 49-77, memoize at 84-102, versionGroupCache) implement overlapping behaviour in one module.
findings.suggestion: Route getVersionGroup through apiGet/fetchJson (it already caches by URL) or build it on memoize, leaving one caching rule to change.

findings.issue: The presentation module imports spriteUrl, which embeds API_BASE_URL and the sprite URL pattern, coupling markup to API configuration.
findings.suggestion: Have callers pass the resolved sprite URL into pokemonCard, or accept it as a dependency parameter, so render.mjs stays free of API knowledge.

findings.issue: section() takes both id and sectionId parameters whose roles are easy to confuse (heading anchor vs element id) — mild flag-parameter creep.
findings.suggestion: Rename to headingId/elementId or fold into one options object with clear names.

summary: A clean, small, layered codebase where most changes land in one findable place: sprites, formatting, sorting and API/caching concerns are each centralized, and htmx partial/full rendering has a proper seam. The main editability tax is that the most-repeated shape — building Pokémon card lists from API references — is copy-pasted with per-view variations, and dead *ByName wrappers plus inconsistent placement of data assembly between server.mjs and views.mjs muddy the intended structure. Most scenarios are 2-file, one-sitting changes; adopting hono/html and one shared card-list helper would push it further.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Self-contained route+view pair (server.mjs:88, views.mjs:250); only cross-links are the Abilities section inside renderPokemonPage, which is built in the same file. Dead renderAbilityPageByName must be spotted or it lingers. No nav links involved.

scenarios.change: Fix wrong sprite on cards for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: All lists render through cardGrid→pokemonCard (render.mjs:79/66) with spriteUrl (api.mjs:46) as the single URL construction point, so one fix covers every list. Caveat: card descriptors carry only {id, name}; if the fix needs the default Pokémon's actual sprite URL from the API rather than the id-pattern, all four list builders would need threading.

scenarios.notes: One file but four separate builders each own their ordering (getHomeData:69, type:152, move:223, ability:258) with three different idioms; there is no shared card-list helper to change once.
